exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Practising for the Exam
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: You look tired, Tom. Have you been practising the piano again?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes. My music exam is next week, and I still can't play one part well.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Don't give up. Remember how badly you played a month ago?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That's true. I have improved a lot, but it's so slow.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Success rarely happens overnight. Just keep practising a little every day.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You're right. I decided to practise one hour each evening until the exam.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: That's the spirit. I'm sure all your hard work will pay off.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Thanks, Mia. I won't stop trying until I get it right.

exercises.translation_cn: 米娅看出汤姆又在练钢琴而疲惫;汤姆下周有音乐考试,有一段还弹不好;米娅劝他别放弃,想想一个月前弹得多差;汤姆承认进步很大但很慢;米娅说成功很少一蹴而就,每天坚持练一点;汤姆决定每晚练一小时直到考试;米娅鼓励他,努力终会有回报。

questions.stem: Why does Tom look tired?
options: He has been practising the piano.
He has been ill all week.

questions.stem: When is Tom's music exam?
What does Mia say about success?
What does Tom decide to do?
options: Ask Mia to play for him.

questions.stem: How does Mia feel about Tom's effort?
options: She thinks it is a waste of time.
She is sure it will pay off.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Success Takes Time
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many people believe that famous writers became successful at once.
In fact, success rarely happens overnight.
A lot of well-known authors faced rejection again and again.
What made them different was that they refused to give up.
So keep trying, and one day your hard work may finally pay off.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多人以为著名作家是一举成名;事实上成功很少一蹴而就;不少知名作家曾一次次遭拒;他们与众不同之处在于不肯放弃;所以请坚持下去,有一天你的努力终会有回报。

questions.stem: What do many people wrongly believe about writers?
options: That they never wrote at all.
That they became successful at once.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about success?
What did many well-known authors face?
What made these authors different?
What advice does the speaker give at the end?
options: Keep trying until it pays off.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Comforting a Friend
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: You look upset, Dawei. Why don't you tell me what's up?

transcript.speaker: Dawei
transcript.text: I ran for Head of the Student Committee, but I wasn't elected.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. I'm sure you did your best.

transcript.speaker: Dawei
transcript.text: I did, but it still hurts. Maybe I'm just not good enough.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Don't say that. You should be proud of how hard you worked.

transcript.speaker: Dawei
transcript.text: Thanks. I suppose one election can't decide everything.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Exactly. Try to look on the bright side and cheer up.

transcript.speaker: Dawei
transcript.text: You're a good friend, Jack. I already feel a little better.

exercises.translation_cn: 杰克看出大伟心烦,问他怎么了;大伟竞选学生会主席却落选;杰克表示遗憾,相信他尽力了;大伟很受伤,觉得自己不够好;杰克让他别这么说,应为努力而自豪;大伟想通一次落选决定不了一切;杰克劝他往好处看、振作起来;大伟感谢这位好友,已经好受了些。

questions.stem: Why is Dawei upset?
options: He was not elected to the committee.

questions.stem: What does Jack say about Dawei's effort?
options: That he is sure Dawei did his best.
That he should have tried harder.

questions.stem: What does Dawei slowly realise?
options: That he will never try again.
That one election can't decide everything.

questions.stem: What does Jack advise Dawei to do?
options: Look on the bright side and cheer up.

questions.stem: How does Dawei feel by the end of the talk?

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 The Swimmer Who Kept Going
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: When Ben first joined the swimming team, he was the slowest of all.
Some of the other boys laughed and told him to quit.
But Ben enjoyed swimming, so he decided to keep practising every day.
Little by little, he grew stronger and faster than before.
Two years later, he won a gold medal at the city games.
exercises.translation_cn: 本刚加入游泳队时是最慢的;有些男孩取笑他,叫他退出;但本喜欢游泳,于是决定每天坚持训练;一点点地,他比以前更强更快;两年后,他在市运动会上夺得金牌。

questions.stem: What was Ben like when he first joined the team?
options: He was the slowest of all.

questions.stem: What did some of the other boys tell him to do?
What did Ben decide to do?
How did Ben change over time?
What did Ben win two years later?
options: A gold medal at the city games.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Two Kinds of Workers
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Lily
transcript.text: Our group project is due on Friday. How is everyone doing?

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: I've already finished my part. I couldn't wait to start.

transcript.speaker: Lily
transcript.text: You really are an eager beaver, Sam. That's a great help.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Thanks. But I'm worried about Leo. He keeps putting off his part.

transcript.speaker: Lily
transcript.text: Yes, he's been dragging his feet all week.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Maybe we should ask him kindly instead of getting angry.

transcript.speaker: Lily
transcript.text: Good idea. A wet blanket helps no one; let's cheer him on.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Agreed. If we stay positive, he might catch our energy.

exercises.translation_cn: 莉莉问小组项目周五截止大家进度如何;萨姆已完成自己的部分,迫不及待就开始了;莉莉夸他是“拼命三郎”,帮了大忙;萨姆担心利奥老是拖着自己那部分;莉莉说他整周都在拖拖拉拉;萨姆建议好言相劝而非发火;莉莉同意,扫兴帮不了人,不如给他打气;萨姆赞同,保持积极也许会感染他。

questions.stem: When is the group project due?
Why does Lily call Sam an eager beaver?
options: Because he finished his part early.

questions.stem: What is the problem with Leo?
options: He keeps putting off his part.

questions.stem: What do Sam and Lily decide to do about Leo?
options: Ask him kindly and cheer him on.

questions.stem: What does Sam hope will happen if they stay positive?

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Use Your Eyes Today
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A famous blind writer once gave us a simple piece of advice.
Use your eyes today as if tomorrow you would lose them.
Look closely at the faces of the people you love.
Listen to the mighty music of an orchestra while you still can.
If we treasure each small thing now, every day becomes a blessing.
exercises.translation_cn: 一位著名的盲人作家曾给我们一个简单的忠告;今天就用好你的眼睛,仿佛明天就会失去它们;仔细看看你所爱之人的脸;趁还能听,去听管弦乐队雄壮的乐声;若我们珍惜眼前的每件小事,每一天都会成为一种福气。

questions.stem: Who gave this piece of advice?
How should we use our eyes today?
options: As if tomorrow we would lose them.
As if we will never need them.

questions.stem: What should we listen to while we still can?
options: The mighty music of an orchestra.

questions.stem: What should we look closely at?
options: The faces of people we love.

questions.stem: What happens if we treasure small things now?
options: We waste a lot of time.
